ai-key.name: AI-Key
ai-key.title: AI Key
ai-key.summary: PoE++ edge-AI appliance adding natural-language search/alerting to Protect (1,800 detections/hr).
gotchas: Not an NVR — it augments an existing Protect console/NVR; you still need recording storage elsewhere.
Needs PoE++ (45 W) — most PoE+ switches/gateway ports can't power it.
Capacity is 1,800 smart detections/hour total across cameras.
$799 — for third-party cameras the $199 AI Port is the cheaper path.
best_for: large Protect sites wanting AI search/alerts

e7-audience-indoor.name: E7-Audience-Indoor
e7-audience-indoor.title: Access Point E7 Audience Indoor
e7-audience-indoor.summary: Directional 12-stream WiFi 7 high-density AP (dual 6 GHz + 5 GHz), 10GbE + redundant GbE, PoE++.

extra.no_2_4ghz: spec lists only 6 GHz (low+high) and 5 GHz radios
extra.no_ip_rating: despite 'Indoor' name, -40C rating; no IP listed

gotchas: No 2.4 GHz radio - legacy/IoT 2.4 GHz-only clients won't connect; add a normal AP for them.
Needs PoE++ (51 W) - PoE+ switches won't run it.
Directional patch antenna, wall/pole mount - for auditoriums/arenas, not general ceiling coverage.
FCC/IC certs only - check regulatory region.
~$1,999: wasted outside true high-density venues; U7 Pro Max / U7 Pro XG cover offices.

e7-audience-us.name: E7-Audience-US
e7-audience-us.title: Access Point E7 Audience
e7-audience-us.summary: Directional indoor/outdoor IP68 WiFi 7 AP: 12 streams on 5+dual 6 GHz, 10GbE + backup GbE, 1,500+ clients.
gotchas: No 2.4 GHz radio — 5 + 6 GHz only; legacy/IoT 2.4 GHz clients need another AP.
Needs PoE++ (51 W max) — a PoE+ switch port won't run it; pair with USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE.
Directional (50°/90° patterns) — for stadiums/auditoriums, not a general ceiling AP (use U7 Pro Max).
10G uplink needs a 10G multi-gig switch port to realize capacity.
US-region SKU; requires a UniFi console/gateway.

e7-campus-indoor.name: E7-Campus-Indoor
e7-campus-indoor.title: Access Point E7 Campus Indoor
e7-campus-indoor.summary: Directional 10-stream WiFi 7 AP for wall/pole mounting in large indoor venues; 10GbE + redundant 1GbE.

requires: 10GbE switch port to use full throughput
UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (10.0.162+)

gotchas: Needs PoE++ (44W max) — PoE+ switches like USW-Pro-8/24-PoE PoE+ ports won't run it; use PoE++ ports or a USW-Pro-Max/ECS PoE++ switch.
Antenna is directional (90°x50°) for wall/pole aiming at a seating area — for normal ceiling omni coverage pick U7 Pro / U7 Pro Max.
To use its 11.5 Gbps 6 GHz radio you need a 10GbE switch port (e.g. USW-Pro-XG-24 class); on 1GbE it's starved.
Indoor-rated (no IP rating) despite pole mounts — outdoor venues need the outdoor E7 Campus variant.
FCC/IC certified only; 6 GHz Extended Range is North America only.

e7-campus-us.name: E7-Campus-US
e7-campus-us.title: Access Point E7 Campus
e7-campus-us.summary: Enterprise indoor/outdoor 10-stream tri-band WiFi 7 AP, directional antennas, 10GbE + backup 1GbE, IP67.
gotchas: Needs PoE++ (44W max) — a PoE+ switch won't run it; use USW-Pro-Max-PoE / ECS class or a PoE++ injector.
Directional antennas (~90°) — not an omni ceiling AP; aim it at the coverage area.
10GbE uplink only pays off on a 10GbE RJ45 switch port.
Pricey ($799) — U7 Outdoor / U7 Pro Outdoor cover ordinary yards.
best_for: campuses, stadium sections, courtyards, high-density outdoor/indoor spaces

e7.name: E7
e7.title: Access Point E7
e7.summary: Enterprise tri-band WiFi 7 AP, 10 streams, 10GbE + redundant GbE uplink, 1000+ clients.
gotchas: Requires PoE++ (43W max) — PoE+ switches/injectors won't run it; use USW-Pro-XG-48-PoE / ECS-24S-PoE / PoE++ ports on Pro Max.
The 10GbE uplink only pays off on a 10G-capable PoE port — on Pro Max 48 PoE's 2.5G ports it's capped at 2.5G.
Redundant port is only 1 GbE; failover drops to 1G.
Overkill for homes; U7 Pro / U7 Pro Max deliver tri-band WiFi 7 on PoE+ for far less.

eah-8.name: EAH-8
eah-8.title: Enterprise Access Hub
eah-8.summary: Enterprise 8-door Access hub: 8 PoE+ reader ports (190 W), 8 lock relays, battery backup.

requires: 32–48V lead-acid battery (optional, not included per spec)

gotchas: Indoor wall-mount steel enclosure (9.1 kg) — needs a comms room, not a door frame.
190 W PoE across 8 reader ports; G3 Intercoms at 13 W are fine, but don't use it as a general PoE switch.
12 V 1 A lock outputs — maglocks over long runs need thicker gauge (spec cable tables).
Battery backup requires a separately sourced 32–48 V lead-acid battery; needs a console running Access.

eav-bridge.name: EAV-Bridge
eav-bridge.title: Enterprise Audio/Video Bridge
eav-bridge.summary: PoE+ AV-over-IP transceiver (encoder or decoder): HDMI 2.0 4K60 + balanced XLR audio, video walls up to 8x8.
gotchas: You need at least two — one as source, one per display/destination.
4K60 over a 1 GbE link means compressed video; 1-to-N needs multicast/IGMP-capable switching (Pro AV profiles on Pro Max/Pro XG).
Requires PoE+ (14W).
Managing app not stated in specs.
best_for: conference rooms, video walls, pro-AV distribution

eav-fiber.name: EAV-Fiber
eav-fiber.title: Switch Enterprise Audio/Video Fiber
eav-fiber.summary: L3 fiber A/V switch: 20x10G SFP+, 2x100G QSFP28, PTPv2 grandmaster/boundary with OCXO + GPS input for ST 2110.

extra.ptp_lag: PTPv2 not supported over aggregated ports

gotchas: No PoE and essentially no copper (one 1GbE) — every endpoint needs SFP+ optics/DACs.
QSFP28 breakout cables are NOT supported, so the 100G ports can't fan out to 4x25G/4x10G.
PTP doesn't run over LAG ports — design media links without aggregation.
Full-depth 1U with 4 hot-swap fans; needs a 4-post rack.
Specialist broadcast/A/V switch — for general 10G aggregation an Aggregation/Pro Aggregation switch is far cheaper.
best_for: broadcast/ProAV facilities needing ST 2110 / Dante / AES67 timing

eav-xg-24-poe.name: EAV-XG-24-PoE
eav-xg-24-poe.title: Switch Enterprise Audio/Video XG 24 PoE
eav-xg-24-poe.summary: 1U full-depth ProAV switch: 24x 10G PoE+++ (90 W) ports, 4x 100G QSFP28, PTP grandmaster/OCXO.

extra.ptp_lag: PTPv2 not supported over aggregated ports

gotchas: PoE budget collapses in redundant-PSU mode: 850 W at 120 V (≈35 W/port across 24) vs 2,150 W shared at 240 V.
Full-depth 9.95 kg chassis — needs a 4-post rack (or center-mount/cantilever on 2-post).
100G QSFP28 breakout cables are not supported — can't fan out to 4x25G.
4 hot-swap fans — not for quiet rooms.
PTPv2 doesn't work over LACP-aggregated ports.
$3,999 ProAV niche — for ordinary 10G PoE edge, USW-Pro-XG-10-PoE is far cheaper.

ecs-24-poe.name: ECS-24-PoE
ecs-24-poe.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 24 PoE
ecs-24-poe.summary: 24-port L3 Etherlighting PoE+++ (90W) campus switch, 16x 10GbE + 8x 2.5GbE, 2x 25G, dual hot-swap PSU.

extra.poe_budget_detail: 1,050W shared w/ (2) stock 600W modules @100-240V; 450W in redundant mode; up to 2,250W shared with optional 1,200W modules @200-240V

gotchas: PoE budget depends on PSU mode: 1,050 W shared but only 450 W in redundant mode with the stock 600 W modules - 24x 90 W needs optional 1,200 W modules.
Full-depth 1U (496 mm) needs a 4-post rack; 4 hot-swap fans - loud, not for a closet near people.
Only 2 uplinks (25G SFP28), modules/DACs not included.
Overkill for home/SMB PoE; USW-Pro-HD-24-PoE gives 24x PoE++ / 600 W for ~40% of the price.
best_for: enterprise wiring closets with WiFi 7 APs/PTZ/PoE lighting

ecs-24s-poe.name: ECS-24S-PoE
ecs-24s-poe.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 24S PoE
ecs-24s-poe.summary: Enterprise 1U L3 stackable switch: 16x 10GbE + 8x 2.5GbE all 90W PoE, 4x 25G, hot-swap PSUs/fans.

extra.qsfp28_note: stacking only, not uplink, no breakout

gotchas: The 2x 100G QSFP28 are stacking-only — no uplink, no breakout; real uplinks top out at 4x 25G SFP28.
Shipped 2x600W PSUs give 1,050W shared but only 450W in redundant mode; 24x 90W needs the 1,200W modules (sold separately).
The 1 GbE RJ45 is OOB management only — not a data port; 10/100M half-duplex unsupported on PoE ports.
Full-depth 1U with 4 hot-swap fans — needs a 4-post rack and is not a quiet closet switch.
Requires UniFi Network 10.6.101+ on your console; stacks only with same-port-count switches.
best_for: campus/enterprise access with WiFi 7 E7-class APs

ecs-24s.name: ECS-24S
ecs-24s.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 24S
ecs-24s.summary: 24-port L3 stackable campus switch: 16x10GbE + 8x2.5GbE copper, 4x25G SFP28, dual PSUs, Etherlighting.

extra.qsfp28_note: 2x 100G QSFP28 are stacking-only, no uplink, no breakout
extra.odd: Hardware lists 'Power Output=yes' but no PoE ports/budget are specified — treated as non-PoE
extra.stacking_rule: up to 4 switches, same port count only

gotchas: No PoE — this is a non-PoE copper switch; for powered 10GbE access use USW-Pro-XG-24-PoE.
The two 100G QSFP28 ports are stacking-only: they cannot be used as uplinks and don't support breakout.
Full-depth 1U (496 mm) — needs a 4-post rack or center-mount shelf; 4 hot-swap fans mean noise.
Stacks only with switches of the same port count (max 4).
best_for: campus distribution with stacking and PSU redundancy

ecs-48-poe.name: ECS-48-PoE
ecs-48-poe.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 48 PoE
ecs-48-poe.summary: 48-port L3 Etherlighting campus switch: 32x10GbE + 16x2.5GbE all 90W PoE+++, 4x25G SFP28, hot-swap PSU/fans.
gotchas: Full-depth 1U (496 mm, 9.5 kg) — needs a 4-post rack or shelf; won't fit a shallow wall cabinet.
2,150W PoE only at 200-240V in shared mode; on 120V it's 1,750W, and with PSU redundancy just 750W — far below 48x90W.
Uplinks are 25G SFP28 only (no 100G) — aggregating several of these needs a 25G-capable aggregation switch.
4 hot-swap fans in a 2,400W-capable chassis: loud; not for offices without a closet.
Requires a UniFi console/gateway running Network 9.0.114+ to adopt.
best_for: campus/enterprise closets with dense WiFi 7 APs and PoE++ devices

ecs-48s-poe.name: ECS-48S-PoE
ecs-48s-poe.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 48S PoE
ecs-48s-poe.summary: 1U 48-port PoE+++ (90W) L3 access switch: 32x 2.5GbE + 16x 10GbE, 4x 25G uplinks, 100G stacking.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (10.6.101+)

extra.qsfp28_note: 2x 100G QSFP28 are stacking-only, no uplink, no breakout

gotchas: PoE budget depends on mains and PSU mode: 2,150W at 240V shared but 1,750W at 120V and only 750W in 120V redundant mode — far below 48x90W.
The 2x 100G QSFP28 are stacking-only; real uplink capacity is 4x 25G SFP28 (100G) for 16x10G + 32x2.5G = 3:1+ oversubscribed.
Stacking only with same-port-count ECS switches, max 4 per stack.
Full-depth 1U with 4 hot-swap fans — equipment-room noise/depth; 4-post rack required.
Needs UniFi Network 10.6.101+; older self-hosted controllers can't adopt it.
best_for: high-density WiFi 7 / 90W PoE (PTZ, displays, lighting) campus closets
not_for: 120V single-circuit closets expecting full PoE budget

ecs-48s.name: ECS-48S
ecs-48s.title: Switch Enterprise Campus 48S
ecs-48s.summary: 48-port L3 stackable Etherlighting campus switch (32x 2.5G, 16x 10G, 4x 25G, 100G stacking); no PoE.

extra.qsfp28_note: 100G QSFP28 ports are stacking-only; no uplink, no breakout
extra.oob_port: (1) 1 GbE RJ45 OOB management only (not counted)
extra.stacking: up to 4 switches, same port count only; cross-stack LAG up to 8 ports

gotchas: No PoE at all ('S' = stacking) - for powered APs/cameras pick ECS-24-PoE or a Pro HD PoE model.
The 2x 100G QSFP28 ports are stacking-only: not usable as uplinks and no breakout cables.
Stacks only with same-port-count switches (max 4) - can't mix with 24-port ECS units.
Full-depth 4-post rack, 4 hot-swap fans - datacenter/closet noise levels.
best_for: dense multi-gig access layers in enterprise closets

ecs-aggregation.name: ECS-Aggregation
ecs-aggregation.title: Switch Enterprise Campus Aggregation
ecs-aggregation.summary: 1U full-depth 48x 25G SFP28 + 6x 100G QSFP28 L3 aggregation switch with MC-LAG, hot-swap PSUs/fans.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (8.5.6+)

extra.routing: spec lists only static + inter-VLAN routing; no OSPF/BGP

gotchas: All-optical: zero RJ45 data ports — every link needs an SFP28/QSFP28 module or DAC (budget it).
QSFP28 breakout is not supported, so the 100G ports cannot fan out to 4x25G.
MC-LAG HA only pairs with a second ECS-Aggregation — true redundancy means buying two.
Full-depth 1U, 340W, 5 hot-swap fans: needs a 4-post rack in a real equipment room, not a closet shelf.
Only static/inter-VLAN routing listed (L3 lite) — no dynamic routing for a true campus core.
best_for: campus distribution layer aggregating many 10/25G access switches

ecs-core.name: ECS-Core
ecs-core.title: Enterprise Campus Switch Core
ecs-core.summary: 1U full-depth 32x 100G QSFP28 L3 core switch (3.2 Tbps) with MC-LAG and hot-swap PSUs/fans.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (10.6.101+)

gotchas: Breakout not supported — 25G/10G devices can't hang off it directly; pair with ECS-Aggregation for 25G fan-out.
MC-LAG requires a second ECS-Core; a single unit is a single point of failure for the whole campus.
100G-only optics on every port; budget QSFP28 transceivers/DACs on top of the switch price.
No dynamic routing listed despite 'core' positioning — static/inter-VLAN only.

ef-core.name: EF-Core
ef-core.title: Enterprise Firewall Core
ef-core.summary: 1U enterprise firewall/gateway: 100G QSFP28, 79 Gbps IPS, 22,500 clients, dual hot-swap PSUs.

requires: SFP28/QSFP28 optics or DACs for fiber ports

extra.routing_throughput_note: 100 Gbps from desc headline, not a spec field

gotchas: Hosts only UniFi Network — no Protect/Access/Talk; cameras need a separate ENVR/UNVR or console.
Shadow Mode HA requires a second EF-Core plus a USW-WAN to split one ISP handoff to both gateways.
Fiber ports (25G SFP28 / 100G QSFP28) ship empty — budget for optics or DACs.
Rack gear with swappable fans and 171 W draw / 585 BTU/hr — loud and hot for a closet; 400 mm deep chassis.
Massive overkill below multi-gig WAN or a few hundred clients — a UCG-Max/UCG-class gateway covers small sites.
not_for: anyone wanting cameras on the same box

efg.name: EFG
efg.title: Enterprise Firewall
efg.summary: 1U 25G enterprise firewall: 12.5 Gbps IPS, 500+ devices/5,000+ clients, Shadow Mode HA, dual hot-swap PSUs.

extra.client_note: Performance may be degraded with advanced gateway features (e.g., Traffic Identification)

gotchas: Hosts only the Network app — no Protect/Access/Talk; cameras/doors need a separate console (UNVR / Cloud Key / UCG-Fiber).
Only 6 ports total (2x 2.5G RJ45, 2x SFP+, 2x SFP28): plan an aggregation/core switch (USW-Pro-Aggregation) behind it.
SFP+/SFP28 ports ship empty — budget for modules or DACs.
True HA (Shadow Mode/VRRP) needs a second EFG.
Single-user WireGuard/Teleport tops out ~1.2 Gbps and IPsec site-to-site ~580 Mbps per tunnel — far below the 12.5 Gbps IPS figure.
Overkill below ~multi-Gbps WAN / hundreds of devices — UCG-Fiber covers 5 Gbps IPS for $279.
not_for: anyone wanting Protect on the gateway

enas.name: ENAS
enas.title: Enterprise NAS
enas.summary: 3U 16-bay enterprise NAS (ZFS RAID-Z), 2x 25G SFP28 + 10GbE, NVMe cache, redundant PSUs, SAS expansion.
gotchas: Sold out at scrape; $3,999 empty - drives are extra.
3U, 16 kg, 4-post rack with square holes required.
25G SFP28 ports need modules/DACs and a 25G/10G switch to matter (e.g. ECS-48S).
Not a Protect NVR - camera storage belongs on a UNVR / console.
best_for: ZFS-style NAS in a UniFi estate

envr-core.name: ENVR-Core
envr-core.title: Enterprise NVR Core
envr-core.summary: 3U enterprise Protect NVR: 16 bays (48 with expansion), 2x 25G SFP28, dual hot-swap PSUs, 300 4K cameras.
gotchas: Hosts Protect/Access/Connect only — no UniFi Network; you still need a gateway/console for the network.
Networking is 2x 25G SFP28 (+1G mgmt) — needs modules/DACs and a 10/25G switch; no 10G+25G mixing across ports.
3U, 23 kg on rails: 4-post square-hole rack required; 10–35°C operating range (server-room only).
Growth beyond 16 drives needs UACC-ESE-16 expansion units listed as 'coming soon'.
Massive overkill under ~60 cameras — UNVR / UNVR-Pro cover small-to-mid sites.

envr.name: ENVR
envr.title: Enterprise NVR
envr.summary: 3U enterprise NVR: 16 drive bays, 70x 4K / 210x HD cameras, dual hot-swap PSUs, 10G networking.
gotchas: Doesn't host UniFi Network — you still need a gateway (UCG/EF) for routing.
Drives not included per specs; 16-bay capacity is HDD-cost dominated.
3U, 16.6 kg, 650–1000 mm 4-post rack rails required.
Huge overkill for <15 cameras — UNVR-Instant or a UCG-Max SSD covers small sites.

u-airwire.name: U-AirWire
u-airwire.title: AirWire
u-airwire.summary: USB-C WiFi 7 client adapter (5/6 GHz, MLO) giving a wired device multi-gig wireless connectivity.

extra.odd: interface reads as a USB-C link presenting 5GbE, not an RJ45 jack

gotchas: It's a client adapter, not an AP - it adds no WiFi coverage.
Wired side is USB-C (USB 3.2 Gen2, 5GbE class), not an RJ45 port - check your device's USB support.
No 2.4 GHz; needs a WiFi 7 UniFi AP to reach multi-gig speeds.
Requires USB-PD 15-20 W power.

u-lte-backup-pro.name: U-LTE-Backup Pro
u-lte-backup-pro.title: UniFi LTE Backup Pro
u-lte-backup-pro.summary: LTE failover modem for UniFi gateways using a BYO AT&T nano-SIM.

extra.thin_specs: no techspecs in source; only description

gotchas: Specs missing in source — verify power/port details before buying.
Requires a UniFi gateway; description specifies AT&T SIM (BYO).
LTE only — U5G-Max-Outdoor offers 5G and dual SIM.
best_for: cheap LTE failover for UniFi gateways

u-lte.name: U-LTE
u-lte.title: UniFi LTE Backup
u-lte.summary: Legacy UniFi LTE Backup: plug-and-play LTE failover for UniFi gateways with bundled AT&T SIM/plan.
gotchas: Not sold in store anymore - current option is U5G-Max (5G, multi-carrier, dual SIM/eSIM).
LTE only and tied to an AT&T SIM/plan per desc.
Needs a UniFi gateway; no specs available in data.

u5g-max-outdoor.name: U5G-Max-Outdoor-US
u5g-max-outdoor.title: UniFi 5G Max Outdoor
u5g-max-outdoor.summary: Outdoor IP67 5G NR modem (3.4 Gbps peak) with directional antennas, dual SIM/eSIM, 2.5GbE PoE.
gotchas: Modem only — requires a UniFi Cloud Gateway/console to act as WAN/failover.
Directional antennas: must be aimed at the tower.
Needs a carrier plan; nano-SIM 2 unusable when eSIM active.
PoE class not specified beyond 'PoE' (14.5W, so 802.3at recommended).
best_for: primary or failover WAN where fixed broadband is poor
not_for: indoor-only installs without a UniFi gateway

u5g-max.name: U5G-Max-US
u5g-max.title: UniFi 5G Max
u5g-max.summary: PoE-powered 5G NR modem (3.4 Gbps), dual SIM/eSIM, 2.5GbE, auto-adopts for UniFi WAN failover.

extra.adoption_note: console must be updated via another WAN before adoption

gotchas: Needs a UniFi gateway - it's a modem, not a router; console must be updated over another WAN before adopting.
Indoor only (0-40 C, no IP rating) - window mount, not mast-mounted.
Data plan/SIM not stated as included; eSIM disables SIM slot 2.
US SKU (band/carrier certs AT&T/T-Mobile/Verizon).
best_for: 5G failover or primary WAN for UniFi sites

u5g-us.name: U5G
u5g-us.title: UniFi 5G Backup
u5g-us.summary: PoE-powered 5G RedCap/LTE backup modem for automatic failover on UniFi gateways.
gotchas: 5G RedCap SA only (no NSA) — peak ~220 Mbps down; a backup link, not a fiber replacement (UDR-5G-Max has full 5G at 3.4 Gbps).
Needs a carrier data plan and a UniFi gateway to fail over.
Indoor (0-40°C) — place near a window for signal.
best_for: automatic WAN failover for small sites

u6-enterprise-iw.name: U6-Enterprise-IW
u6-enterprise-iw.title: Access Point U6 Enterprise In-Wall
u6-enterprise-iw.summary: In-wall WiFi 6E AP, 10 streams tri-band, 2.5GbE uplink, 4-port GbE switch with one PoE out.

requires: PoE++ source for PoE output (PoE+ otherwise)

gotchas: PoE passthrough port only works if the AP is fed PoE++; PoE+ powers the AP alone.
WiFi 6E, not WiFi 7 — no 320 MHz/MLO.
Built-in switch ports are 1 GbE; only the uplink is 2.5G.
Requires a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.
best_for: hotel rooms, dorms, offices with wall jacks
adding wired ports + 6 GHz per room
not_for: ceiling coverage of large open areas

u6-enterprise.name: U6-Enterprise
u6-enterprise.title: Access Point U6 Enterprise
u6-enterprise.summary: Ceiling WiFi 6E AP: 10 streams, tri-band incl. 6 GHz 4x4, 2.5GbE uplink, PoE+.
gotchas: Needs PoE+ (22 W) - 802.3af ports (e.g. UDR) won't run it.
2.5GbE uplink - a 1G switch port caps it; pair with a 2.5G PoE+ switch.
WiFi 6E, not WiFi 7 - for new installs U7 Pro / U7 Pro Max add MLO and 320 MHz at similar cost.
2.4 GHz is only 2x2.

u6-extender.name: U6-Extender-US
u6-extender.title: Access Point U6 Extender
u6-extender.summary: Wall-plug WiFi 6 mesh extender (5 GHz 4x4, 2.4 GHz 2x2), no Ethernet; discontinued.

requires: an existing wired UniFi AP to mesh from

gotchas: Legacy, not in store; current WiFi 7 mesh options are UX7 nodes or the U7-Mesh.
No Ethernet port — wireless backhaul only, so throughput is roughly halved vs. a wired AP.
Needs a wired UniFi AP + console to mesh from; no 6 GHz.
Region-specific plug (US SKU).
best_for: filling a dead spot where no cable can run

u6-iw.name: U6-IW
u6-iw.title: Access Point U6 In-Wall
u6-iw.summary: In-wall WiFi 6 AP for single rooms with a built-in 4-port GbE switch (1 PoE out).

requires: PoE+ source if using PoE output
UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (6.0.45+)

gotchas: Only one downstream port supplies PoE, and only when the AP itself is fed PoE+.
Everything (WiFi + 4 wired ports) shares a single 1GbE uplink.
WiFi 6 only — no 6 GHz; consider a WiFi 7 wall AP if 6 GHz clients matter.
Mounts over a wall box; coverage 115 m² — one per room, not a whole-floor AP.
best_for: hotel rooms, dorms, offices with wired desk devices

u6-lr.name: U6-LR
u6-lr.title: Access Point U6 Long-Range
u6-lr.summary: Previous-gen ceiling WiFi 6 AP with 4x4 radios for extended range; no 6 GHz, GbE uplink.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (6.0.45+)

extra.ip54_note: IP54 listed but it's an indoor ceiling AP

gotchas: Not in store / previous gen — the WiFi 7 replacement is the U7 Long-Range (or U7 Pro).
No 6 GHz band (WiFi 6, not 6E).
1GbE uplink caps aggregate throughput.
Needs PoE+; 802.3af switches won't power it.

u6-mesh-pro.name: U6-Mesh-Pro
u6-mesh-pro.title: Access Point U6 Mesh Pro
u6-mesh-pro.summary: Indoor/outdoor IPX6 WiFi 6 AP with high-gain antenna, GbE passthrough, PoE adapter included.
gotchas: Only 4 streams (2x2 per band) and GbE uplink — capacity is modest despite the 'Pro' name.
No 6 GHz; outdoor WiFi 7 needs the E7/U7 Outdoor line.
IPX6 (water) rating — no dust rating digit.
Passthrough port: data only per spec (no PoE out stated).
Requires a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.

u6-mesh.name: U6-Mesh
u6-mesh.title: Access Point U6 Mesh
u6-mesh.summary: Slim indoor/outdoor IPX5 WiFi 6 AP (6 streams) for mesh, wall/pole mount, PoE (adapter included).
gotchas: IPX5 only (water jets, no dust rating) - for exposed sites check against IP66/67 outdoor APs.
No 6 GHz; WiFi 6 only.

No 6 GHz, 1 GbE uplink.

ubb-xg.name: UBB-XG
ubb-xg.title: Building-to-Building Bridge XG

uc-ev-station-lite.name: UC-EV-Station-Lite

uc-ev-station-pro.name: UC-EV-Station-Pro
uc-ev-station-pro.title: EV Station Pro

Single-phase only.

usw-16-poe.summary: Fanless 1U L2 16x 1GbE switch, 8 PoE+ ports sharing a tiny 42W budget, 2x 1G SFP.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (7.2.94+)

gotchas: 42W total PoE across 8 PoE+ ports — roughly two U7 Pros (21W each) and nothing else.
Only 8 of 16 ports supply PoE.
1G SFP uplinks only, no 10G — the whole switch shares a 1G pipe to the core.
Layer 2 only; no inter-VLAN routing.
Upside: fanless/silent.
best_for: quiet 1G closet with a handful of low-power PoE devices

usw-24-poe.name: USW-24-POE
usw-24-poe.title: Switch 24 PoE
usw-24-poe.summary: Fanless 24-port 1GbE L2 switch with 16 PoE+ ports, 95W budget, 2x1G SFP.
gotchas: Only 95W PoE for 16 PoE ports — ~6W/port average; three U7 Pro-class APs (~22W each) eat most of it. USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE has 400W.
Uplinks are 1G SFP only — the whole switch shares a 1Gbps uplink; no 10G.
All 1GbE; WiFi 7/6E APs will bottleneck at 1G.
Layer 2 only — inter-VLAN routing stays on the gateway.
best_for: quiet closets with a few low-power PoE devices (cameras, phones)

usw-24.name: USW-24
usw-24.title: Switch 24
usw-24.summary: Fanless 1U Layer 2 24x GbE switch with 2x 1G SFP; no PoE.
gotchas: Uplinks are 1G SFP only — no 10G SFP+; whole switch funnels through 1 Gbps to the core (USW-Pro-24 / Pro Max 24 fix).
No PoE — APs/cameras need USW-24-PoE or a separate injector/switch.
Layer 2 only; inter-VLAN routing happens on the gateway.
Needs a UniFi console/gateway to adopt (Network 7.2.94+).

usw-48-poe.name: USW-48-POE
usw-48-poe.title: Switch 48 PoE
usw-48-poe.summary: 1U fanless L2 switch: 48x 1G (32 PoE+), 4x 1G SFP, 195 W budget.
gotchas: Only 32 of 48 ports supply PoE, and 195 W is ~6 W/port if all 32 are loaded.
Uplinks are 1G SFP — no SFP+, so the whole 48-port switch shares 1 Gbps (or a 4G LAG) upstream; USW-Pro-Max-48-PoE fixes this.
All copper is 1 GbE — no multi-gig for WiFi 6E/7 APs.
L2 only — inter-VLAN routing stays on the gateway.
Requires a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.

usw-48.name: USW-48
usw-48.title: Switch 48
usw-48.summary: Fanless 48-port GbE L2 switch with 4x 1G SFP uplinks; no PoE.
gotchas: Uplinks are 1G SFP only - 48 GbE clients share at most 4 Gbps (LACP) to the core; get USW-Pro-Max-48 for 10G SFP+.
No PoE - for APs/cameras use a PoE model.
Layer 2 only - inter-VLAN routing stays on the gateway.
No multi-gig ports.

usw-aggregation.name: USW-Aggregation
usw-aggregation.title: Switch Aggregation
usw-aggregation.summary: 8-port 10G SFP+ L2 rack switch for aggregating 10G uplinks between switches/servers.
gotchas: All 8 ports are SFP+ cages with no RJ45 — every link needs an SFP+ module, DAC, or 10GBASE-T module.
Layer 2 only — no inter-VLAN routing; L3 aggregation needs a USW-Pro-class L3 switch or the gateway.
Only 8 ports and 1000 VLANs; a 24-port 10G/25G core (e.g. USW-Pro-XG / ECS line) for bigger cores.
Needs a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.
best_for: 10G backbone between a gateway, NAS and several PoE switches

usw-enterprise-24-poe.name: USW-Enterprise-24-PoE
usw-enterprise-24-poe.title: Switch Enterprise 24 PoE (Vintage)
usw-enterprise-24-poe.summary: Vintage 24-port L3 PoE+ switch: 12x1G + 12x2.5G all PoE+, 400W, 2x10G SFP+.
gotchas: Legacy/not in store — modern replacement is USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE (Etherlighting, PoE++).
PoE+ only (30W class) — no PoE++/802.3bt for U7 Pro Max/E7 class APs or PTZ cameras.
400W across 24 ports = ~16.7W/port average if all loaded.
Half the ports are 1GbE only — put WiFi 6E/7 APs on the 12 2.5G ports.
best_for: existing deployments expanding with a matching unit

usw-enterprise-48-poe.name: USW-Enterprise-48-PoE
usw-enterprise-48-poe.title: Switch Enterprise 48 PoE (Vintage)
usw-enterprise-48-poe.summary: Vintage 1U L3 switch: 48x 2.5G PoE+ ports, 4x SFP+, 720 W budget.
gotchas: Marked Vintage and not in store — current replacement is the USW-Pro-Max-48-PoE family.
PoE+ only (32 W max/port) — no PoE++/802.3bt for U7 Pro XG / E7 / PTZs.
48x 2.5G into 4x 10G SFP+ = 3:1 oversubscription at line rate.
Single PSU; redundancy only via USP-RPS.

usw-enterprise-8-poe.name: USW-Enterprise-8-PoE
usw-enterprise-8-poe.title: Switch Enterprise 8 PoE (Vintage)
usw-enterprise-8-poe.summary: Compact L3 switch: 8x2.5GbE all PoE+ (120W) with 2x10G SFP+ uplinks.

extra.vintage: titled '(Vintage)' but still priced in store
extra.acl_limits: IPv4 ACL 12, MAC ACL 10 (much lower than rack models)

gotchas: Marked 'Vintage' — superseded by the Pro Max 16 PoE / Pro HD line; expect no new features.
120W for 8 PoE+ ports = 15W/port average; PoE+ only, no PoE++.
SFP+ uplinks need modules/DACs; no 10GbE RJ45.
Very small ACL tables (12 IPv4 / 10 MAC) vs 128 on rack siblings.
best_for: small office/desk multi-gig PoE for 2.5G APs with 10G fiber uplink

usw-flex-2-5g-5.name: USW-Flex-2.5G-5
usw-flex-2-5g-5.title: Switch Flex Mini 2.5G
usw-flex-2-5g-5.summary: Tiny 5-port 2.5GbE managed switch powered by USB-C or PoE; no PoE output.
gotchas: No 10G uplink — all 5 ports share 2.5G, so it's a desk switch, not an aggregation point.
Can't power anything: no PoE output (it can be PoE-powered itself).
Basic L2 (no LACP/802.1X/IGMP snooping listed).
Adopts only via a UniFi console running Network 8.6.9+.

usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe.name: USW-Flex-2.5G-8-PoE
usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe.title: Switch Flex 2.5G PoE
usw-flex-2-5g-8-poe.summary: Compact 8x 2.5GbE PoE++ switch with 10G RJ45/SFP+ combo uplink; powered by PoE+++ or 210W adapter.

extra.combo_uplink: 10GbE RJ45 and SFP+ are one combo port (only one usable)

gotchas: PoE output depends on input: 196 W only with the separately-sold 210 W adapter; 76 W from PoE+++ (802.3bt) input, just 16 W from PoE+.
The 10GbE RJ45 and SFP+ are a combo - one uplink only.
AC adapter not included; out of the box it needs a PoE+++ upstream port.
Lighter L2 feature set (256 VLANs, no LACP listed).
best_for: remote rooms fed by one 10G PoE+++ run
not_for: dense PoE++ loads on PoE input

usw-flex-2-5g-8.name: USW-Flex-2.5G-8
usw-flex-2-5g-8.title: Switch Flex 2.5G
usw-flex-2-5g-8.summary: Compact 8x 2.5GbE switch with 10G RJ45/SFP+ combo uplink, powered by USB-C or PoE+ input.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (9.0.114+)

extra.combo: 10GbE RJ45 and SFP+ are one combo port — only one usable at a time
extra.missing_features: no LACP, IGMP snooping, 802.1X or ACLs listed; 256 VLANs

gotchas: Does not output PoE — can't power APs/cameras; it consumes PoE+.
The 10GbE RJ45 and SFP+ are a single combo uplink — one or the other, not both.
Lite feature set: no LACP, IGMP snooping or 802.1X in specs.
DIN and magnetic mounts sold separately; powering over PoE needs an 802.3at (PoE+) source.
best_for: multi-gig desk/AV cabinet off one 10G drop

usw-flex-mini.name: USW-Flex-Mini
usw-flex-mini.title: Switch Flex Mini
usw-flex-mini.summary: Tiny 5-port GbE managed switch powered by PoE or 5V USB-C; desk/room expansion.
gotchas: No PoE output — can't power APs/cameras; it consumes PoE on one port.
Minimal L2 feature set: no STP/RSTP, 802.1X or LACP listed — loops are on you.
1 GbE only; for 2.5G/10G desks use USW-Flex-XG.
USB-C needs a 5V/1A adapter (5W) if not PoE-fed; still needs a UniFi console to manage VLANs.

usw-flex-xg.name: USW-Flex-XG
usw-flex-xg.title: Switch Flex XG
usw-flex-xg.summary: Compact 5-port L2 switch: 4x 10GbE + 1x GbE, powered by PoE+ or 5V/5A USB-C.
gotchas: No SFP+ — 10G uplink must be copper 10GbE (Cat6a); fiber needs a different switch (USW-Aggregation / Flex 2.5G variants).
No PoE output; it can only be powered BY PoE+ (or a 5V 5A USB-C supply, included 25W adapter).
Only 4 ports are 10GbE; the 5th is 1 GbE.
Needs a UniFi console to adopt; small ACL tables (12 IPv4 / 10 MAC).

usw-flex.name: USW-Flex
usw-flex.title: Switch Flex
usw-flex.summary: 5-port 1G outdoor-capable L2 switch powered by PoE++, passing 4 PoE+ outputs (46 W).

extra.outdoor: 'Outdoor Ready=yes' but no IP rating given

gotchas: Output budget scales with input: 46 W only from PoE++/60 W injector (sold separately); PoE+ gives 20 W, PoE 8 W.
Per-port PoE output capped at 25 W — below full 802.3at 30 W.
All 1 GbE, no SFP; single 1G uplink for every downstream device.
Outdoor-ready but no IP rating listed; pole mount needs the USW-Flex-Utility accessory.
Very minimal L2 feature set (no STP/LACP/802.1X listed).
best_for: extending one PoE++ run to a few cameras/APs outdoors

usw-flexutility.name: USW-Flex-Utility
usw-flexutility.title: Switch Flex Utility
usw-flexutility.summary: Outdoor weatherproof enclosure plus 54V PoE adapter for housing a Switch Flex.
gotchas: It's only an enclosure + PoE adapter — the Switch Flex itself is sold separately.
Needs AC mains at the install point to feed the 54V adapter.
No IP rating published; fitment is stated only for 'Switch Flex' — verify before using other Flex models.
not_for: anyone expecting a switch in the box

usw-industrial-din-2-5g-8-poe.name: USW-Industrial-DIN-2.5G-8-PoE
usw-industrial-din-2-5g-8-poe.title: Switch Industrial DIN 2.5G 8 PoE
usw-industrial-din-2-5g-8-poe.summary: Upcoming DIN-rail industrial 8-port PoE++ switch: 4x2.5GbE + 4x1GbE, 2x SFP+, redundant power.

extra.thin_data: no techspecs; all fields from one-line desc
extra.poe_note: desc: '8-port PoE++ switch' — assumed all 8 RJ45 ports PoE++, unverified

gotchas: Coming soon with no published techspecs — PoE budget, power input type and temperature range are unknown.
Only 4 of 8 copper ports are 2.5GbE.
DIN-rail form factor needs a cabinet/enclosure and a DIN PSU; not a desktop switch.

usw-industrial-din-8-poe.name: USW-Industrial-DIN-8-PoE
usw-industrial-din-8-poe.title: Switch Industrial DIN 8 PoE
usw-industrial-din-8-poe.summary: Hardened DIN-rail 8x 1G PoE++ (60 W) switch, 2x 1G SFP, dual DC inputs, up to 480 W.

extra.budget_note: Max 480W, based on power supply capability

gotchas: Power supply NOT included — the 480 W budget only materializes with a 50–57 V DC supply big enough to deliver it.
Uplinks are 1G SFP only (no SFP+).
All copper 1 GbE — no multi-gig.
Status ComingSoon at time of scrape.
Requires a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.
best_for: industrial cabinets, extreme temps, DIN-rail panels

usw-industrial-din-8.name: USW-Industrial-DIN-8
usw-industrial-din-8.title: Switch Industrial DIN 8
usw-industrial-din-8.summary: Hardened DIN-rail 8x GbE L2 switch with 2x 1G SFP, dual 12-60V DC inputs, -30 to 70 C.
gotchas: No PoE output - can't power cameras/APs; pair with a DC PoE source.
DC terminal-block power only and the PSU isn't included.
1 GbE / 1G SFP only - no multi-gig.
Status ComingSoon at time of scrape; no IP rating, so outdoor use needs an enclosure.

usw-industrial.name: USW-Industrial
usw-industrial.title: Switch Industrial
usw-industrial.summary: Hardened fanless 10-port 1GbE L2 switch, 8 PoE++ ports, 430 W, -40 to 60 C; discontinued.

extra.port_note: spec lists 1 GbE RJ45=10 (8 PoE++); no SFP listed
extra.limited_l2: fewer L2 features (no LACP/802.1X/IGMP listed), 256 VLANs

gotchas: Legacy, not in store — the USW-Industrial-DIN-2.5G-8-PoE is the coming replacement (adds 2.5GbE + SFP+).
1GbE only with no SFP uplink listed — bottleneck for 8 PoE++ devices.
Stripped L2 feature set (no LACP/802.1X listed, 256 VLANs) vs. other UniFi switches.
No IP rating listed despite 'industrial' — still needs an enclosure outdoors.
best_for: hot/cold plant rooms powering 60 W PTZ/APs

usw-lite-16-poe.name: USW-Lite-16-PoE
usw-lite-16-poe.title: Switch Lite 16 PoE
usw-lite-16-poe.summary: Fanless 16-port 1GbE L2 switch with 8 PoE+ ports and a small 45 W budget.
gotchas: Only 45 W PoE total for 8 PoE+ ports — about 3 WiFi 6/7 APs or a handful of cameras before you run out.
No SFP/SFP+ and no 2.5GbE — 1G uplink bottleneck and APs capped at 1G.
Layer 2 only.
Needs a UniFi console/gateway to adopt; for more PoE budget step up to USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE.
best_for: quiet desk/closet with a few PoE devices

usw-lite-8-poe.name: USW-Lite-8-PoE
usw-lite-8-poe.title: Switch Lite 8 PoE
usw-lite-8-poe.summary: Fanless 8-port 1GbE L2 desktop switch, 4 PoE+ ports, 52 W budget via external 60 W brick.
gotchas: Only 4 of 8 ports supply PoE; 52 W budget depends on the included external 60 W adapter.
1GbE only — no SFP or 2.5GbE uplink for multi-gig APs/WAN.
Layer 2 only; external power brick is a single point of failure.
best_for: small office/home: a couple of APs + cameras

usw-mission-critical.name: USW-Mission-Critical
usw-mission-critical.title: UPS PoE Switch Mission Critical
usw-mission-critical.summary: 9-port GbE L3 switch with built-in 368 Wh battery giving uninterruptible PoE to 8 devices (120 W).

extra.conflict: Layer 3=yes but no L3 feature section listed

gotchas: All ports are 1 GbE and no SFP - 1G uplink; can't feed multi-gig WiFi 7 APs at full speed.
Only 120 W PoE across 8 ports (4 PoE+ / 4 PoE++) - runtime/budget sized for a few critical APs/cameras, not a closet.
Heavy (9 kg) and 480 mm deep - needs a 4-post rack.
Costs ~$999 for 9 ports; a regular PoE switch + USP-RPS or a real UPS may fit better.
best_for: keeping a few cameras/APs/door hubs alive through outages

usw-pro-24-poe.name: USW-Pro-24-POE
usw-pro-24-poe.title: Switch Pro 24 PoE
usw-pro-24-poe.summary: 1U L3 24x 1GbE PoE switch (16 PoE+, 8 PoE++), 2x 10G SFP+ uplinks, 400W budget.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (5.10.5+)

extra.ipv4_static_routes: spec says 2 (vs 256-512 on siblings) — likely data error

gotchas: All 24 access ports are 1GbE — 2.5GbE WiFi 7 APs (U7 Pro) are capped; USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE adds 2.5GbE PoE ports.
400W budget vs 16x30W + 8x60W = 960W theoretical — you can't max every port.
Older generation (2020-era, Network 5.10 baseline) superseded by the Pro Max line with Etherlighting and multi-gig.
Spec lists only 2 IPv4 static routes — treat its L3 as very limited.
best_for: 1G PoE closet with a few 60W devices

usw-pro-24.name: USW-Pro-24
usw-pro-24.title: Switch Pro 24
usw-pro-24.summary: 24-port 1GbE L3 non-PoE fanless rack switch with 2x10G SFP+; no longer in store.

extra.odd: IPv4 Static Routes = 2 (vs 256 on siblings) — likely a data error or very limited L3

gotchas: Not sold in the store anymore (legacy) — look at the current Pro Max 24 non-PoE for a new build.
No PoE at all — APs/cameras need a separate PoE switch or injectors.
1GbE-only copper; static-route table listed as only 2 entries, so L3 is minimal.

usw-pro-48-poe.name: USW-Pro-48-POE
usw-pro-48-poe.title: Switch Pro 48 PoE
usw-pro-48-poe.summary: 48-port 1GbE L3 PoE switch (40 PoE+, 8 PoE++), 4x10G SFP+, 600 W budget; previous Pro generation.

extra.generation_note: still sold but no 2.5GbE / no Etherlighting — superseded in features by Pro Max line

gotchas: All copper ports are 1GbE — no 2.5GbE for WiFi 7 APs; the Pro Max 48 PoE line adds 2.5GbE + Etherlighting.
600 W over 48 PoE ports averages 12.5 W/port; only 8 ports are PoE++.
No 802.3bt; 4x SFP+ uplinks require modules/DACs.
Fan-cooled 1U 400 mm deep — not a living-space device.
best_for: dense 1G PoE closets (phones, cameras, WiFi 6 APs)

usw-pro-48.name: USW-Pro-48
usw-pro-48.title: Switch Pro 48
usw-pro-48.summary: Legacy fanless 1U L3 48x GbE switch with 4x 10G SFP+; no PoE. Not in store.
gotchas: Not sold in store (legacy) — modern replacement is USW-Pro-Max-48 / Pro Max 48 PoE.
All 48 copper ports are 1 GbE only — no 2.5G for WiFi 7 APs.
No PoE output; the PoE twin (USW-Pro-48-PoE) or Pro Max 48 PoE is needed for APs/cameras.
Fanless (good for quiet spaces) but MAC table 16k and 4 MB buffer vs 32k on Pro XG.

usw-pro-8-poe.name: USW-Pro-8-PoE
usw-pro-8-poe.title: Switch Pro 8 PoE
usw-pro-8-poe.summary: Compact L3 8x 1GbE PoE switch (6 PoE+, 2 PoE++ 64W), 2x 10G SFP+, 120W budget.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (7.5.176+)

gotchas: 120W budget vs 6x32W + 2x64W = 320W theoretical — two PoE++ devices plus a few APs exhausts it.
Access ports are 1GbE only — 2.5GbE WiFi 7 APs are capped.
Internal PSU with no RPS/redundancy option.
best_for: small closet/desk with 10G uplink feeding a few APs or a PTZ

usw-pro-aggregation.name: USW-Pro-Aggregation
usw-pro-aggregation.title: Switch Hi-Capacity Aggregation
usw-pro-aggregation.summary: 1U L3 aggregation switch: 28x 10G SFP+ and 4x 25G SFP28 for core/backbone.
gotchas: Zero RJ45 ports — every link needs an SFP+/SFP28 module, DAC, or 10GBASE-T module (RJ45 10G modules run hot).
No PoE — it's a backbone; edge PoE comes from USW-Pro-Max/Enterprise switches below it.
Single internal PSU; redundancy needs the separate USP-RPS.
Requires a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.
L3 is 'lite': static routes + inter-VLAN only, no OSPF/BGP.
best_for: 10G core for multiple PoE switches / NAS

usw-pro-hd-24-poe.name: USW-Pro-HD-24-PoE
usw-pro-hd-24-poe.title: Switch Pro HD 24 PoE
usw-pro-hd-24-poe.summary: 24-port L3 Etherlighting PoE++ switch: 22x 2.5G + 2x 10G RJ45 (all PoE++), 4x 10G SFP+, 600 W.
gotchas: 600 W budget vs 24x 64 W ports (1,536 W) - fine for APs, not for all-PoE++ loads.
No 802.3bt Type 4 / 90 W - for 90 W devices use ECS-24-PoE.
Only 2 ports are 10 GbE RJ45; WiFi 7 APs with 10G uplinks beyond 2 need SFP+ or another switch.
400 mm deep - check shallow wall racks.

usw-pro-hd-24.name: USW-Pro-HD-24
usw-pro-hd-24.title: Switch Pro HD 24
usw-pro-hd-24.summary: 24-port L3 Etherlighting switch: 22x2.5G + 2x10GbE RJ45, 4x10G SFP+, no PoE.
gotchas: No PoE — APs and cameras need a PoE sibling (USW-Pro-HD-24-PoE) or injectors.
Only 2x 10GbE RJ45; the rest of copper is 2.5GbE, so it's not a 10G copper access switch.
Per-port cost is high vs USW-Pro-Max-24 if you don't need 2.5G everywhere.
Requires Network 9.0.114+ on a UniFi console.

usw-pro-max-16-poe.name: USW-Pro-Max-16-PoE
usw-pro-max-16-poe.title: Switch Pro Max 16 PoE
usw-pro-max-16-poe.summary: Compact L3 Etherlighting switch: 12x 1G PoE+, 4x 2.5G PoE++, 2x SFP+, 180 W.
gotchas: Only 4 ports are 2.5G — the 12 others are 1 GbE; WiFi 7 APs beyond 4 get bottlenecked.
180 W budget across 16 PoE ports (~11 W avg) — fine for APs/cameras, not 16x PoE+ loads.
1U rack mounting needs the separate Rack Mount accessory.
External power brick, no RPS/redundant input.
SFP+ ports need modules/DACs; requires a UniFi console to adopt.
best_for: home/SMB core with a few WiFi 7 APs

usw-pro-max-16.name: USW-Pro-Max-16
usw-pro-max-16.title: Switch Pro Max 16
usw-pro-max-16.summary: 16-port L3 Etherlighting switch (12x 1G + 4x 2.5G, 2x 10G SFP+), USB-C powered, desk/wall/rack.

requires: UniFi OS console / gateway running UniFi Network (8.1.127+)

extra.rack_mount: 1U rack requires add-on Rack Mount accessory

gotchas: No PoE at all despite the 'Pro Max' name — for APs/cameras buy the USW-Pro-Max-16-PoE.
Only 4 of 16 ports are 2.5GbE; the other 12 are 1GbE.
Powered by an external 25W USB-C brick — no internal PSU or RPS backup.
Rack ears are a separate accessory.
best_for: desk/media-cabinet switch with a 10G uplink and a few multi-gig clients

usw-pro-max-24-poe.name: USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE
usw-pro-max-24-poe.title: Switch Pro Max 24 PoE
usw-pro-max-24-poe.summary: 24-port L3 Etherlighting PoE++ switch: 16x1GbE + 8x2.5GbE, all PoE (16 PoE++), 2x10G SFP+, 400 W.
gotchas: Only 8 of 24 ports are 2.5GbE — WiFi 7 APs beyond 8 will be stuck at 1G.
400 W budget across 24 PoE ports (16 PoE++ @60 W) — can't drive many 60 W devices at once.
No 802.3bt Class 8 (90 W) — that needs USW-Pro-XG-24-PoE.
Uplinks are 2x 10G SFP+ (no 10GbE RJ45) — needs modules/DACs; single PSU unless you add USP-RPS.
best_for: small/medium office with a few WiFi 7 APs

usw-pro-max-24.name: USW-Pro-Max-24
usw-pro-max-24.title: Switch Pro Max 24
usw-pro-max-24.summary: 24-port L3 Etherlighting switch: 16x1G + 8x2.5G RJ45, 2x10G SFP+, no PoE.
gotchas: No PoE at all — for APs/cameras pick USW-Pro-Max-24-PoE.
Only 8 of 24 ports are 2.5GbE; 16 are 1GbE — WiFi 7 APs on 1G ports will bottleneck.
No 10GbE RJ45; 10G only via 2 SFP+ (modules/DACs extra) — USW-Pro-HD-24 adds 10GbE copper.
Needs a UniFi console/gateway to adopt.
best_for: rack edge switch for wired desks/servers with Etherlighting

usw-pro-max-48-poe.name: USW-Pro-Max-48-PoE
usw-pro-max-48-poe.title: Switch Pro Max 48 PoE
usw-pro-max-48-poe.summary: 1U L3 Etherlighting 48-port PoE switch: 32x 1G + 16x 2.5G, 720W PoE (16 PoE++), 4x 10G SFP+.
gotchas: Only 16 of 48 ports are 2.5GbE (32 are 1G) — WiFi 7 APs on 1G ports are uplink-bottlenecked.
Only 16 ports are PoE++ (64W); the other 32 are PoE+ (32W) — count your E7/U7 Pro Max/PTZ loads.
720W budget < 48 x 32W; can't run every port at max PoE+.
Uplinks are 4x 10G SFP+ (no 25G); for 10GbE copper + 90W PoE step up to USW-Pro-XG-48-PoE.

usw-pro-max-48.name: USW-Pro-Max-48
usw-pro-max-48.title: Switch Pro Max 48
usw-pro-max-48.summary: 48-port L3 Etherlighting switch (16x 2.5G + 32x 1G) with 4x 10G SFP+ uplinks; no PoE.
gotchas: No PoE - APs/cameras need USW-Pro-Max-48-PoE or a separate PoE switch.

gotchas: Legacy G3, not in store — the G5 Flex is the direct replacement (2K, AI detections).
1080p@25fps, no smart detections; 10/100 Ethernet.
Requires UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage.

uvc-g3-ins.name: UVC-G3-INS
uvc-g3-ins.title: Camera G3 Instant
uvc-g3-ins.summary: Legacy compact 1080p WiFi Instant camera, two-way audio, USB powered; not in store.

extra.power_note: 5V 2A USB adapter included; Instant PoE adapter optional

gotchas: Legacy / not in store — G6 Instant (4K, AI, IPX5) replaces it.
1080p, no smart detections listed; indoor only (no IP rating).
WiFi-only; requires Protect console/NVR.

uvc-g4-bullet.name: UVC-G4-Bullet
uvc-g4-bullet.title: Camera G4 Bullet
uvc-g4-bullet.summary: Legacy 2K indoor/outdoor bullet, IPX4, 9 m IR, 24 fps.
gotchas: Legacy, not in store — G5 Bullet is the cheaper, current replacement.
24 fps and IPX4 only.
Needs Protect on a console/NVR.

uvc-g4-dome.name: UVC-G4-DOME
uvc-g4-dome.title: Camera G4 Dome
uvc-g4-dome.summary: Legacy 2K (4MP) PoE dome, 24 FPS, IR 9m, IPX4/IK08; not in store.
gotchas: Legacy / not in store — G5 Dome / G6 / AI Turret replace it.
IPX4 only: covered outdoor locations, not exposed.
2K at 24 FPS, IR just 9m; no face/LPR AI.
Needs Protect on a console/NVR with storage.

uvc-g4-doorbell-pro-poe-kit.name: UVC-G4 Doorbell Pro PoE Kit
uvc-g4-doorbell-pro-poe-kit.title: G4 Doorbell Pro PoE Kit
uvc-g4-doorbell-pro-poe-kit.summary: PoE G4 Doorbell Pro with package camera, NFC reader, plus PoE chime; plug-and-play kit.
gotchas: Needs Ethernet + PoE at the door (and a 2nd PoE run for the chime) — not wired-transformer powered.
Sold out; FHD (2MP) only vs 5MP on the newer G6 Entry.
IPX4 — sheltered doorways only.
Requires Protect on a console/NVR; NFC door unlock also needs Access + hardware.

uvc-g4-doorbell-pro.name: UVC-G4 Doorbell Pro
uvc-g4-doorbell-pro.title: G4 Doorbell Pro
uvc-g4-doorbell-pro.summary: WiFi video doorbell with dual cameras (main + package), display, NFC and two-way intercom.

requires: strong WiFi at the door (or UACC-Adapter-DBPOE for wired GbE)
UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage (e.g. UCG-Max w/ SSD, UNVR-Instant, ENVR)

Needs 16–24 V AC doorbell wiring (or USB-C); chime compatibility is limited to listed models.

Requires UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage.

uvc-g4-ins.name: UVC-G4-INS
uvc-g4-ins.title: Camera G4 Instant
uvc-g4-ins.summary: Compact WiFi 2K camera, USB-C powered, two-way audio, wide angle, IPX5.

Not battery-powered: needs USB-C 5V/2A at the mount.
Short 6 m IR; older G4 generation.
Needs Protect on a console/NVR.

uvc-g4-pro.name: UVC-G4-Pro
uvc-g4-pro.title: Camera G4 Pro
uvc-g4-pro.summary: Legacy 4K bullet with 3x optical zoom, IP67, 15 m IR, 50 fps.

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage

gotchas: Discontinued (not in store) - G6 Bullet / G6 Edge Turret are the current 4K replacements with face/LPR.
Only 15 m IR - weaker night range than G6 models (30-40 m).
No face/LPR recognition listed.
Requires Protect on a console/NVR.

uvc-g5-bullet.name: UVC-G5-Bullet
uvc-g5-bullet.title: Camera G5 Bullet
uvc-g5-bullet.summary: Budget 2K indoor/outdoor bullet, IP55, AI detections, 9 m IR, mic.

Mic only, no speaker; IK04 is not vandal-resistant.

uvc-g5-dome-ultra.name: UVC-G5-Dome-Ultra
uvc-g5-dome-ultra.title: Camera G5 Dome Ultra
uvc-g5-dome-ultra.summary: Tiny indoor 2K PoE dome, IK06, 20 m IR, basic AI detections.
gotchas: Indoor only (no IP rating) — use G6 Turret outdoors.
2K, not 4K; no face/LPR recognition; no audio listed.
Previous G5 generation — G6 Turret is 4K for $70 more.

uvc-g5-dome.name: UVC-G5-Dome
uvc-g5-dome.title: Camera G5 Dome
uvc-g5-dome.summary: 2K ceiling dome with AI detections, two-way audio, 9 m IR, IPX4 when covered.
gotchas: Only IPX4 'while covered' — eaves/porches only, not exposed outdoors.
2K and 9 m IR; no face/LPR — G6 line adds 4K + recognition.
Requires Protect on a console/NVR with storage.
best_for: indoor/covered-porch general coverage on a budget

uvc-g5-flex.name: UVC-G5-Flex
uvc-g5-flex.title: Camera G5 Flex
uvc-g5-flex.summary: Small 2K PoE camera for indoor or covered outdoor use with basic AI detections.

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage (e.g. UCG-Max w/ SSD, UNVR-Instant, ENVR)

extra.ports_note: single 10/100 RJ45 (not representable in ports schema)

gotchas: 10/100 Ethernet only and 2K resolution — budget camera, not 4K.
IPX4 only while covered — not for exposed outdoor spots (pick AI Dome/G6).
Only 6 m IR; no LPR/face recognition.
Requires UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage.

uvc-g5-pro.name: UVC-G5-Pro
uvc-g5-pro.title: Camera G5 Pro
uvc-g5-pro.summary: 4K indoor/outdoor bullet with 3x optical zoom, 25-40m IR, AI detections.

requires: UniFi Protect host (Cloud Gateway/UNVR/CloudKey) with storage

extra.power_note: PoE alone; PoE+ with Vision Enhancer (12.95W)

gotchas: Vision Enhancer (40m IR) bumps it to PoE+.
IK04 — low vandal resistance; G6/AI line for IK10.
No face/LPR — AI-series cameras for recognition.
Needs Protect host with storage.

uvc-g5-ptz.name: UVC-G5-PTZ
uvc-g5-ptz.title: Camera G5 PTZ

requires: UniFi Protect host (Cloud Gateway/UNVR/CloudKey) with storage

gotchas: Only 2x optical zoom — a framing PTZ, not long-range; G6 Pro 360/AI line for coverage, bigger PTZ for distance.
Pan is 350°, not continuous 360°.
IK04 — low vandal resistance; mic only.
Needs PoE+ and a Protect host.

uvc-g5-turret-ultra.name: UVC-G5-Turret-Ultra
uvc-g5-turret-ultra.title: Camera G5 Turret Ultra

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage

gotchas: Requires Protect on a console/NVR - no onboard storage.
2K only, no face/LPR - for those step to G6 Bullet/Dome.
10/100 port, mic only (no speaker), small 1/2.4" sensor.
IK04 only - not vandal-resistant like the G6 Dome (IK10).

uvc-g6-180.name: UVC-G6-180
uvc-g6-180.title: Camera G6 180
uvc-g6-180.summary: Dual-sensor 16MP 180° panoramic PoE+ camera with AI (face/LPR), IR 20m, IP66.
gotchas: Needs UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage — no standalone recording to cloud.
Requires PoE+ (15W); 20 FPS max, not 30.
10/100 network port — fine for the stream but no GbE.
IK04 only — not vandal-resistant; AI Turret (IK08) for reachable mounts.

uvc-g6-bullet.name: UVC-G6-Bullet
uvc-g6-bullet.title: Camera G6 Bullet
uvc-g6-bullet.summary: 4K bullet with 1/1.8" sensor, Multi-TOPS AI (face/LPR), 30 m IR, IP66, PoE.

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage

gotchas: Requires Protect on a console/NVR with storage.
Fixed wide lens - LPR works at short range only; for long range use AI PTZ.
10/100 port, mic only, IK04 (not vandal-proof - G6 Dome is IK10).

uvc-g6-dome.name: UVC-G6-Dome
uvc-g6-dome.title: Camera G6 Dome
uvc-g6-dome.summary: Vandal-proof IK10 4K dome with 1/1.8" sensor, Multi-TOPS AI (face/LPR), 30 m IR, PoE.

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage

gotchas: Requires Protect on a console/NVR with storage - no local recording.
10/100 Mb port - fine for one stream, no GbE.
Microphone only, no speaker / two-way audio.
Fixed lens, no optical zoom - for zoom use G6 Edge Turret / AI PTZ.

uvc-g6-edge-bullet.name: UVC-G6-Edge-Bullet
uvc-g6-edge-bullet.title: Camera G6 Edge Bullet

IK04 — not vandal-rated; G6 Edge Dome is IK10.
Status ComingSoon at time of scrape.
Standalone storage is 128 GB; long retention wants a Protect NVR.

uvc-g6-edge-dome.title: Camera G6 Edge Dome
uvc-g6-edge-dome.summary: Vandal-proof IP66/IK10 4K dome, 1/1.2" sensor, 2.36x optical zoom, onboard AI + 128 GB edge storage.

Standalone mode records to the 128 GB microSD; long retention still wants a Protect NVR.
Mic only — no speaker/two-way audio (G6 Edge Bullet has two-way).
$699 vs $199 G6 Turret — pay for the big sensor/zoom only if low light or distance matter.

uvc-g6-edge-turret.name: UVC-G6-Edge-Turret
uvc-g6-edge-turret.title: Camera G6 Edge Turret
uvc-g6-edge-turret.summary: Premium 4K turret, 1/1.2" sensor, 2.36x optical zoom, two-way audio, 128 GB onboard - works standalone.

Standalone retention is just the 128 GB card; a Protect NVR is still needed for longer history.
$699 - G6 Bullet/Dome give 4K + LPR for far less if you don't need zoom/low-light sensor.
Only 2.36x zoom - for long range use UVC-AI-PTZ.

uvc-g6-entry.name: UVC-G6-Entry

requires: UniFi Protect + UniFi Access on console
UniFi Access Hub / Hub Mini (for NFC & door control)

gotchas: Requires PoE+ (16W).
NFC and door-release need a UniFi Access Hub / Hub Mini, and both Protect and Access installed on the console.
Package camera runs at 3 FPS — stills, not video.
IR only 5m; IP55 (sheltered entry recommended).

gotchas: WiFi-only (802.11ac) — 4K streams need a strong AP signal; no RJ45.
Powered by 5V/2A USB-C; PoE requires the PoE-to-USB-C adapter (not included).

IR only 6m — short-range night vision.

uvc-g6-mini-dome.name: UVC-G6-Mini-Dome
uvc-g6-mini-dome.title: Camera G6 Mini Dome

Pan/tilt/zoom is digital (fisheye dewarp), not optical — detail at distance is limited; G5 PTZ for real PTZ.
24 fps max and only 15m IR.
Spec lists a 10/100 interface for a 12MP stream — odd; verify.

uvc-g6-pro-bullet.name: UVC-G6-Pro-Bullet
uvc-g6-pro-bullet.title: Camera G6 Pro Bullet

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage (e.g. UCG-Max w/ SSD, UNVR-Instant, ENVR)

gotchas: Needs PoE+ (802.3at).
IK04 only — not vandal-proof; G6 Pro Dome is IK10.
60 m IR needs the separate Vision Enhancer accessory; base IR is 40 m.

uvc-g6-pro-dome.name: UVC-G6-Pro-Dome
uvc-g6-pro-dome.title: Camera G6 Pro Dome

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage (e.g. UCG-Max w/ SSD, UNVR-Instant, ENVR)

uvc-g6-pro-entry.name: UVC-G6-Pro-Entry

requires: UniFi Protect AND UniFi Access on the console
UniFi Access Hub / Hub Mini for NFC & lock

gotchas: NFC and door-lock features require a UniFi Access Hub / Hub Mini.
Both Protect and Access must be installed on the console.
PoE+ (18W) required — not plain PoE.

uvc-g6-pro-turret.name: UVC-G6-Pro-Turret
uvc-g6-pro-turret.title: Camera G6 Pro Turret

requires: UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage (e.g. UCG-Max w/ SSD, UNVR-Instant, ENVR)

gotchas: Needs PoE+ (802.3at); won't run off UNVR-Instant's 802.3af ports.
Only IK04 — not vandal resistant; pick the G6 Pro Dome (IK10) for reachable mounts.
Requires UniFi Protect on a console/NVR with storage.

uvc-g6-ptz.name: UVC-G6-PTZ
uvc-g6-ptz.title: Camera G6 PTZ
uvc-g6-ptz.summary: Outdoor 4K dual-lens PTZ, 10x hybrid zoom, AI face/LPR tracking, 30 m IR, PoE+.
gotchas: Needs PoE+ (24.5W) — 802.3af won't power it.
'10x' is hybrid: 5x optical + 2x digital.
Pan is 350°, not continuous 360°; IK04 not vandal-rated.

uvc-g6-turret.name: UVC-G6-Turret
uvc-g6-turret.title: Camera G6 Turret
uvc-g6-turret.summary: $199 IP66 4K turret, 1/1.8" sensor, AI face/LPR, plain PoE.
gotchas: Requires a Protect console/NVR with storage — no onboard recording listed (G6 Edge models have 128 GB).
10/100 Mbps network port, fixed lens, no optical zoom.
IK04 only — not vandal-resistant (G6 Edge Dome is IK10).
Mic only, no speaker.
best_for: general 4K exterior coverage on a budget

uwb-xg.name: UWB-XG
uwb-xg.title: WiFi BaseStation XG
uwb-xg.summary: Stadium-class WiFi 5 BaseStation: 3x 5 GHz 4x4 radios (12 streams), beamforming array, IP67, 10GbE.

extra.odd: Channel Bandwidth lists HE (WiFi 6) modes but WiFi Standard says WiFi 5

gotchas: 5 GHz ONLY — no 2.4 GHz radio, so older/IoT 2.4 GHz-only clients can't connect.
WiFi 5 generation (no 6 GHz/WiFi 6E/7) despite the high price.
Needs PoE++ (adapter included) and a 10GbE path to use full capacity.
Directional, 3.2 kg venue gear — not a home or office AP.

ux.name: UX
ux.title: UniFi Express
ux.summary: Tiny USB-C Cloud Gateway + WiFi 6 AP for very small networks; Network app only, 4 devices.

extra.software_note: Network 9.0 is the last major train; 9.1+ requires UniFi Express 7

gotchas: Not in store / legacy: Ubiquiti says Network 9.1+ needs UniFi Express 7 — buy UX7 instead.
Only 1 WAN + 1 LAN at 1GbE and no IDS/IPS listed — gigabit-ish ISP ceiling, no security inspection.
Manages just 4 UniFi devices and hosts Network only (no Protect/Access) — outgrow it with UCG-Ultra/Max.
No PoE output; any AP or switch beyond it needs its own power.
best_for: meshing as an extra AP in an existing UniFi network

ux7.name: UX7
ux7.title: UniFi Express 7
ux7.summary: Puck-sized gateway with integrated tri-band WiFi 7 AP, 10GbE WAN, 2.5GbE LAN; meshes with more UX7 nodes.
gotchas: Only one WAN port (Max WAN = 1): no dual-ISP failover except via UniFi LTE Backup — UCG-Max supports 4 WANs.
Single 2.5GbE LAN port — anything more than one wired device needs a switch.
10G WAN port, but IDS/IPS is 2.3 Gbps; multi-gig plans lose speed with IPS on.
Hosts Network only: no Protect/Access/Talk, so cameras need a UCG-Max/UNVR.
Only 4 SSIDs per radio and 2x2 radios; USB-C powered (no PoE in or out).
best_for: apartments / small homes wanting gateway + WiFi 7 in one puck
